title: Classic Krusty — The Sane Society

source.notes: Complete discussion from the user-designated local transcript inputs/fromm-1958/transcript.txt (1958-05-25). Wallace recast as Krusty; network announcements, nonverbal stage directions, and obsolete next-week promotion omitted. Minor transcription spacing/typo corrections recorded in edit-map.json. All substantive questions and answers retained, including the final discussion of socialism, war, and hope. Long answers split into short sequential takes without added inter-take pauses. Historical assertions remain in their 1958 context. Two late transcript slips are corrected against transcription of the original recording: twenty or thirty years; a mass man. The initial synthesis dialogue is retained in synthesis-script.json. Two Krusty cues are lightly adapted for clear delivery: the introductory question is reordered, and the book-title cue adds Your book. All changes are recorded in edit-map.json.

disclosure: Unofficial fan parody. AI animation and recreated Krusty and Erich Fromm voices. Based on the May 25, 1958 Mike Wallace interview; host recast and broadcast framing edited. Not authentic archival audio.

turns.text: By meaning and interest in work - maybe I'm pressing this unnecessarily hard - what specifically do you mean? When a man works at a factory, with a monkey wrench, let us say, what meaning, what, what deeper meaning are you looking for?
